title: Postern app
description: One self-hosted app Postern knows. The folder name is the app id.

label.description: The app's name as people write it.

auth.description: How the app takes its key. Give each way it accepts. null when Postern cannot send its key (then give a note).

header.description: The header the key goes in, such as X-Api-Key.

query.description: The URL parameter the key goes in, such as apikey.

authz.description: An Authorization header scheme: bearer for a token, basic for a user name and password.

keyHint.description: Where the key is found in the app, as a menu path: 'Settings → General → Security → API Key'.

note.description: Shown instead of a key suggestion, for an app Postern can recognise but not send a key to.

match.description: How the app's own page gives it away. Checked against the page the upstream address returns, with no extra request.

title.description: Lower-case words found in the page <title>, as whole words.

body.description: Exact strings found in the page, such as 'window.Sonarr'. At least 6 characters, so they do not match other apps.

header.description: A response header only this app sends.

probe.description: A public endpoint that confirms the app and reports its version. It is sent without the upstream key.

path.description: Relative to the upstream address, without a leading slash. May carry a query.

discover.description: Also try this probe when the page named no app. Only a few paths may do this, so keep it for endpoints that answer without a key and that several installs leave unbranded.

json.description: Top-level fields of a JSON answer, each with one test.

jsonKeys.description: The JSON answer must have exactly these top-level keys.

version.description: Where the version is: a top-level JSON field, or a regex whose first group is the version.

icon.description: Where icon.svg comes from. LICENSES/<source>.txt must hold its licence.
